blocking: Nothing is currently reported as blocked or missing — the blocked-signals field is empty. EP-3 (hasql keyset engine) is actively building on the now-complete EP-1 core types; EP-2 (servant surface) has not started yet but is independent of EP-3 and can proceed in parallel since both depend only on EP-1, which is done. EP-4 (conformance suite) and EP-5 (guides/release readiness) are simply queued behind EP-3's engine API and the rest of the work respectively, per the declared integration points — not stalled by any flagged issue.
status: The plan is progressing on schedule: the foundational scaffold/core package (EP-1) is complete, the hasql keyset engine (EP-3) is actively underway, and the servant surface, conformance suite, and guides (EP-2, EP-4, EP-5) remain queued to start with no reported blockers.
what: The plan builds a small family of Haskell packages, decomposed along package/dependency boundaries: a dependency-light core defining wire types and a versioned opaque cursor format; a servant package providing a RelayPage combinator with server/client/link and OpenAPI 3.1 support; a hasql package implementing the keyset-pagination engine (predicate generation, ORDER BY/LIMIT n+1, hasNextPage/hasPreviousPage derivation, backward-page reversal) driven by a declarative sort specification; a conformance suite that consuming services can run to prove no-skip/no-duplicate behavior; and developer/agent-facing guides — all following the shared Haskell conventions recorded in the repo's ADRs.
why: Hand-rolling Relay-style cursor pagination on top of servant and hasql is easy to get subtly wrong in ways that silently break infinite scrolling — the reference implementation in mls-service-v2 demonstrates every failure mode this plan exists to eliminate: lossy text/float cursor round-tripping that skips or duplicates rows at page boundaries, a discarded has_more flag that reports a phantom next page, backward pagination that violates Relay's required edge ordering, ~150 lines of copy-pasted per-table pagination SQL, and a non-spec request surface. This initiative exists to replace all of that with a single, reusable, spec-correct library.
